title: Cream Cheese vs Sour Cream: Which Has More Fat and Calories?

seo.title: Cream Cheese vs Sour Cream: Nutrition
seo.meta_description: Regular cream cheese often has about 33–35 g of fat and 330–350 calories per 100 g, versus roughly 18–20 g and 190–210 calories for full-fat sour cream.
seo.search_intent: Compare cream cheese and sour cream by fat, calories, protein, and culinary use.

excerpt: Regular cream cheese is usually much more concentrated: about 33–35 g of fat and 330–350 calories per 100 g, versus roughly 18–20 g of fat and 190–210 calories in full-fat sour cream.
content_html:
Cream cheese and sour cream share tang and dairy richness, but cream cheese is much more concentrated. Regular cream cheese often lands around 330–350 calories and 33–35 g of fat per 100 g, compared with roughly 190–210 calories and 18–20 g of fat for full-fat sour cream.

Water explains much of the gap

Cream cheese is a concentrated spreadable cheese; sour cream remains a cultured cream with more water. Removing or binding more water packs more fat and solids into the same 100 g.

A tablespoon still shows the difference

Fifteen grams of regular cream cheese is roughly 50 calories and 5 g of fat. The same weight of full-fat sour cream is closer to 30 calories and 3 g of fat. Exact labels vary.

Neither is a major protein food

Cream cheese can provide around 5–7 g of protein per 100 g, somewhat more than many sour creams, but a normal serving is small. Fat remains the dominant macronutrient.

Texture can matter more than nutrition in a recipe

Cream cheese thickens frosting, dips, and sauces aggressively. Sour cream adds acidity and creaminess while staying more fluid. A straight swap can change both mouthfeel and structure.

The useful rule

Sour cream is usually the less calorie-dense choice by weight; cream cheese is the denser choice when the recipe needs body and spreadability.

faq.question: Which has more calories, cream cheese or sour cream?
faq.answer: Regular cream cheese usually has substantially more calories and fat by the same weight.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Cream cheese generally has a little more, but typical servings of either are not major protein sources.

faq.question: Can I substitute one for the other?
faq.answer: Sometimes, but cream cheese is much denser while sour cream is more fluid and tangy.
